Analytic Jacobians

Source: R/jacobians.R
robot_jacobian_analytic.Rd

Maps joint velocities to the time derivative of the position and a minimal orientation parameterization. With representation = "rpy" the orientation is the roll-pitch-yaw triple \((r, p, y)\) with \(R = R_z(y) R_y(p) R_x(r)\), and \(\omega = E(r, p, y) (\dot r, \dot p, \dot y)\) with columns \(E = [R_z R_y e_x, R_z e_y, e_z]\); the analytic Jacobian is \(J_a = \mathrm{diag}(I, E^{-1}) J\). E is singular when \(\cos p = 0\); the function stops there. With representation = "rotvec" the orientation is the rotation vector \(\phi\) and \(\dot\phi = J_l(\phi)^{-1}\omega\).

robot_jacobian_analytic(
  robot,
  q,
  frame = NULL,
  representation = c("rpy", "rotvec"),
  tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

q

Configuration.

frame

Frame name (NULL for the end effector).

representation

"rpy" or "rotvec".

tol

Singularity tolerance on \(|\cos p|\).

Value

A 6 by n matrix.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("puma560")
robot_jacobian_analytic(robot, c(0, 0.3, -0.2, 0.1, 0.4, 0.2))
#>          joint1        joint2        joint3        joint4     joint5     joint6
#> x     0.1500500 -5.592750e-01 -4.316694e-01 -1.314306e-19  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> y     0.3896048  2.385641e-17 -1.402801e-18 -1.387779e-17  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> z     0.0000000  3.896048e-01 -2.290948e-02 -1.318705e-20  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> roll  0.0000000 -3.682612e-01 -3.682612e-01 -1.067785e-01 -0.2601764 -0.5250239
#> pitch 0.0000000 -9.455240e-01 -9.455240e-01  3.250100e-02 -0.9731390  0.1186888
#> yaw   1.0000000  1.721395e-01  1.721395e-01  1.044917e+00  0.1315832  1.1231933
